title: Homepage claims 'largest' inventory with no source to back it up
quote: Measurable claim 'largest' with no visible substantiation/source.
statute: CA Business & Professions Code §17508
recommendation: Either show where 'largest' comes from (for example a dated BMW of North America ranking) or change it to wording that is not a measurable claim, like 'a deep selection of new and certified BMWs in the San Gabriel Valley.'

title: 2026 BMW X5 page shows a monthly payment with no total amount payable
quote: Monthly payment advertised on the 2026 BMW X5 (new, VIN 5UX13EU08T9238938) page without the total amount payable over the term.
statute: Cal. Civ. Code §1784.41(c)(1) (CARS Act, SB 766) | CALIFORNIA controls: CARS Act (SB 766, Cal. Civ. Code §1784.20 et seq.), operative Oct 1, 2026. The federal FTC CARS Rule (16 CFR Part 463) was VACATED by the 5th Circuit (Jan 2025) and formally WITHDRAWN from the CFR (Fed. Reg. Feb 2026), not enforceable; FTC Section 5 still applies. Pin-cites verified against the chaptered statute (leginfo) 2026-06-28; CNCDA Compliance Guide v1.2 (2026-08-07) and Webinar FAQ (2026-08-31) folded in 2026-09-14.
recommendation: Under the CARS Act (operative Oct 1, 2026) any written monthly-payment representation must also disclose the total the consumer will have paid after all scheduled payments, plus any assumed down payment or trade value. CNCDA: an ad for an identified unit that states a payment also needs that unit's total price; the safest practice is total price only, payments reserved for desked terms.

title: 'In-Transit' vehicles on new inventory with no arrival date shown
quote: 'In-Transit' shown on the new inventory page with no arrival or delivery information captured.
statute: FTC Act §5; FTC Automobile Industry Pricing Transparency FAQs (Sept. 2026) Q10; FTC staff remarks 2026-09-30
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION: confirm the unit has actually shipped, add the arrival information the store can support, and confirm it is not allocated to another customer's paid order (FTC FAQ Q10; FTC staff 2026-09-30). The arrival date may sit in a widget the crawl missed.

title: 9 of 33 homepage images have no alt text for screen readers
quote: 9 of 33 homepage images missing alt text.
statute: ADA Title III; Cal. Civ. Code §51 (Unruh); WCAG 2.1 1.1.1
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION: have the web vendor confirm which homepage images are decorative. Add descriptive alt text to every image that carries meaning. Missing alt text is the most commonly cited issue in serial ADA/Unruh dealer-website suits.

title: 3 of 4 homepage form fields have no label for screen readers
quote: 3 of 4 form fields have no associated label/aria-label.
statute: ADA Title III; Cal. Civ. Code §51 (Unruh); WCAG 2.1 1.3.1/4.1.2
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION: have someone tab through the homepage lead form with a screen reader and confirm each field is announced. Ask the web vendor to give every field a proper label. Unlabeled lead-form fields are a frequent ADA/Unruh claim.

title: Homepage has no skip-to-content link
quote: Homepage structure gaps: no skip-to-content link (WCAG 2.4.1).
statute: ADA Title III; Cal. Civ. Code §51 (Unruh); WCAG 2.1
recommendation: Add a skip-to-main-content link. A quick fix that closes easy ADA/Unruh exposure.

title: Same 330i shown with two different lease deals and prices on the specials page
quote:

$3,535 due at signing

$0.25/mile over 10,000 miles/year
Lease this New 2026 BMW 3 Series 330i NA (Model: 263Y, VIN: 3MW69CW09T8G84983). MSRP: $50,600.00. Total Price before rebates (gross capitalized cost): $50,722. $439 per month for 39 months with $5,498.80 due at signing
up to $0.25 per mile over 7500 miles per year
statute: CA Vehicle Code §11713(a), §11713.1(e); CA Civil Code §1784.40(d) (CARS Act, operative 2026-10-01)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION: The crawl captured the offer-details window text and the offer card text for the same VIN with different payment, due at signing, price and mileage figures. A shopper who sees $47,940 and 10,000 miles a year can hold the store to the better terms, so one VIN should carry one price and one set of lease terms everywhere on the site.

title: Lease offers give a purchase option price but never label the residual value
quote:
Option to purchase vehicle at lease end is $39,758.
Option to purchase at lease end: $25,786.80.
statute: Regulation M 12 CFR §213.7(d); CA Vehicle Code §11713.16
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION: Same issue as last month. The newer offer cards now show an adjusted capitalized cost, which is progress, but no offer labels the residual value, and the offer-details window offers show neither. Add a labeled residual value (and adjusted capitalized cost to the details-window offers) to every lease disclosure template.

$429

Disclosure
Lease this New 2026 BMW 2 Series 228
Total of Payments (scheduled monthly payments): $16,713.84.
statute: CA Vehicle Code §11713.16(i); CA Civil Code §1784.41(c)(1) (CARS Act, operative 2026-10-01); Regulation M 12 CFR §213.7(d)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION: Same pattern as last month, now with the CARS Act live. The card shows the monthly payment and due at signing up front, but the total of payments, mileage limit and other lease terms only appear after the Disclosure section is opened. Ask the vendor to print the total of payments and mileage allowance on the card face next to the payment so they do not depend on a click. Verify on desktop and mobile whether the Disclosure text is visible by default.

title: Specials use shortened 'tax and license' wording instead of the required added-costs sentence
quote:
Selling price $66,900. Tax, title, and license are extra.
Doc Fee:$85
Plus tax and license. $4875 Due At Signing
statute: CA Vehicle Code §11713.1(c)(2); CA Civil Code §1784.41(f)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION: Same issue as last month, now on the specials page. The details-window offers show a selling price with the doc fee listed separately and only 'Tax, title, and license are extra.' Where a price leaves out the doc fee, use the exact statutory sentence: 'Plus government fees and taxes, any finance charges, any dealer document processing charge, any electronic filing charge, and any emission testing charge.' Where the doc fee is already inside the price (as on the newer cards), drop the doc fee reference so the wording is not misleading.

title: Lease specials use 39-month and 7,500-mile terms instead of BMW's 36-month, 10,000-mile standard
quote:
$429 per month for 39 months
up to $0.25 per mile over 7500 miles per year
statute: BMW Brand Guidelines for Retail (March 2026) — Pricing: Lease/Finance Offers Attribution
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION: Same as last month. BMW retail guidelines call for 36-month, 10,000-mile lease advertising. Confirm with the BMW market team whether the 39-month / 7,500-mile structures are approved for co-op; if not, rebuild the featured offers on the 36/10,000 structure (some current lease cards already use 36 months).

title: Due-at-signing breakdown lists no bank acquisition fee; confirm none is collected
quote: The amount due at signing includes the first monthly payment of $429, a $4,446.00 down payment does not include necessary tax, title and license fees, and a $0.00 security deposit.
statute: FTC Pricing Transparency FAQs Q8; Regulation M 12 CFR §213.7
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION: The card's due-at-signing amount equals the down payment plus first payment only, and no lease acquisition fee is itemized anywhere on the card. The older details-window offers show about $1,010 more at signing than down plus first payment, which suggests a fee is collected on those. Confirm with the F&I manager whether a BMW Financial Services acquisition fee is charged on these deals; if it is, it must be inside the advertised due-at-signing or the capitalized cost.

title: Homepage offer slides depend on a pop-up window for their disclosures
quote: Offer Details and Disclaimers
statute: CA Vehicle Code §11713.16(i); Regulation M 12 CFR §213.7
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION: Same as last month. The homepage offer slides carry only an 'Offer Details and Disclaimers' link; no offer terms were captured as page text. Check each slide: any payment or price on the slide image needs the key terms (term, due at signing, total price, expiration) on the slide itself, not only in the pop-up.

title: Homepage promises 'the best rates' with no support
quote:
some of the most competitive financing or lease plans of any car dealer in Alhambra.
Competitive Financing: Access to the best rates and flexible lease plans
statute: CA Business & Professions Code §17508
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION: Same as last month. 'The best rates' reads as a factual claim. Change it to something the store can back up, such as 'Competitive rates through BMW Financial Services and local lenders.'

title: Site banner says browsing the site means agreeing to an arbitration provision
quote:
By continuing to use this site, you agree to our Privacy Policy, which includes an Arbitration Provision
NOTICE: This Privacy Policy Contains an Agreement to Arbitrate Disputes and a Class Action Waiver.
statute: CA Civil Code §1784.21, §1784.22 (CARS Act, operative 2026-10-01)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION: Any term that limits a buyer's CARS Act rights is void, and a browse-to-agree arbitration and class waiver tied to the website could be read as reaching vehicle-purchase disputes. Have dealer counsel review the arbitration agreement linked from the privacy policy and add a carve-out stating it does not waive or limit any right under the CARS Act or the sales contract.

title: Homepage copy uses 'afford' price language BMW asks dealers to avoid
quote: we’re confident you’ll find the vehicles you’re looking for at a price you can afford.
statute: BMW Brand Guidelines for Retail (March 2026) — Ad Copy: Prohibited Language and Terms
recommendation: Same as last month. Replace with brand-safe copy, for example 'we're confident you'll find the BMW that fits the way you drive.'

title: Homepage copy says 'car' where BMW requires 'vehicle'
quote:
Wide Variety of New and Used Cars for Sale
your new car, but we’re not like most dealers.
statute: BMW Brand Guidelines for Retail (March 2026) — Ad Copy: Vehicle vs Car Terminology
recommendation: Same as last month. Swap 'car' for 'vehicle' in the homepage SEO copy and inventory page headings (for example 'Used Cars for Sale in Alhambra, CA' and the 'Courtesy Car' badge).

Total Price After Incentives
$70,547

statute: FTC Pricing Transparency FAQs Q5, Q9; CA Vehicle Code §11713.1(e)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION: The specials page lists the $2,000 on this same X5 (VIN 5UX13EU03T9300505) as a 'BMWFS Lease Credit', which only lease customers get, yet the inventory card subtracts $2,000 from the cash price for everyone. Confirm what each 'Incentive' line actually is. Any incentive tied to BMW FS financing or leasing must come out of the 'after incentives' figure on the cash price, and the boilerplate 'pricing includes all offers and incentives' should be rewritten to name the rebate and who qualifies.

Ask the website vendor to rename 'Total Price After Incentives' to 'Net Cost After BMW Rebate' and label the rebate line by source on every new inventory card and vehicle page.
